motion: Should school uniforms be mandatory?
text: Whether school uniforms should be mandatory is similar to asking whether street clothes should be allowed in schools. Depending on a person’s perspective, the answers can be very different. Parents who support uniforms may argue that school is about being a student before being an individual. Students who support uniforms might argue that when everyone dresses similarly, it removes many of the preconceptions people form about one another. Instead of recognizing someone by their clothes or hairstyle, students are encouraged to actually get to know each other — recognizing people by their voice, personality, or mannerisms, and perhaps truly seeing them beyond appearance. Uniforms can also reduce visible class distinctions. Students are less likely to be perceived as wealthy or poor based on their clothing. While some may still know about another student’s background, it is no longer immediately reflected in their appearance at school. In schools without uniforms, students often feel pressure to dress in ways that help them assimilate into particular social groups. Uniforms can lessen that pressure by creating a more equal and consistent standard of appearance, making social conformity less tied to fashion and economic status.

motion: Should sex workers or consumers be penalized?
text:
Sex workers and their clients should not be criminally penalized because criminalizing consensual adult transactions often creates more harm than it prevents. The existence of prostitution is not eliminated by prohibition; instead, it is pushed into an unregulated black market where oversight, health protections, and worker safety become significantly more difficult to maintain.
The moral objection to prostitution often centers on the involvement of money, but financial considerations exist throughout human relationships. Adults form relationships for many reasons, including attraction, companionship, security, and economic stability. Society generally does not criminalize relationships simply because one person benefits financially from the other. The central questions should be consent, coercion, exploitation, and harm—not simply whether money is involved.
A regulated framework does not require society to celebrate or promote sex work; it recognizes that criminal law is a poor tool for controlling private consensual behavior. Regulation allows governments to address actual harms by creating health standards, improving safety, allowing workers to report abuse, and making trafficking and coercion easier to identify.
Criminalization often produces unintended consequences because it is based on treating a complex social issue as a moral violation rather than a practical policy problem. By forcing the activity underground, society may unintentionally strengthen the very conditions it seeks to prevent: exploitation, unsafe environments, and lack of accountability. The question should not be whether prostitution fits a particular moral ideal, but whether criminalization actually creates a safer and more ethical outcome.

motion: Should governments subsidize renewable energy?
text:
Governments should subsidise for a number of reasons:
Firstly, according to the laws of microeconomics, governments should intervene if a market failure occurs, in this case there would be a positive externality of consumption occurring. This would mean that the good or service provides more benefits than is represented by the market mechanism. In order to prevent a collapse of the market and total market failure, governments should intervene in order to increase the consumption of this good as it is socially beneficial. 
Leading on from that, renewable energy is socially beneficial and can be considered to be a national investment. The energy usage of a nation determines their manufacturing abilities, infrastructure etc and therefore as fossil fuel reserves are continually being used up (as well as what could be considered the international duty of protection of the environment, also meaning that their consumption should be reduced) investments in renewable energy sources can help to provide long term energy resilience. It means that nations are not subject to inflationary prices due to geopolitical tensions, as well as ensuring that COP targets are adhered to. Due to the specific advantages to the nation collectively, governments should subsidise as it produces a national social benefit which exceeds the marginal private benefit.

motion: Is online education as effective as traditional classroom learning?
text:
I believe online education has a much weaker effect on students' learning than tradition classroom learning. However, it still has its benefits. Firstly, online learning can be useful as it is very easily accessed by students. Students can go through their lessons anywhere and anytime in their own homes, saving them time, money and effort. Moreover, it can be beneficial as it increases students' dependancy on technology and allows them to use their phones and laptops in a rather productive matter. Technology remains a key part of our daily and future lives, and the more youth students get used to it, the easier it would be for them in the future.

However, unfortunately technology by most of the youth is utilized for the wrong purposes. Rather than using it for research, debate-making and educational benefits, students have gotten used to using it for social media, online games and endless scrolls to fulfil their entertainment. Now don't get me wrong online learning is great and all, but it can be very easily exploited by younger students. In my personal experience, almost every classmate I know has admitted to sleeping amidst their online lessons during the COVID-19 Pandemic, as well as using AI to cheat in their online lessons. 

Therefore, online education strongly challenges students' credibility and ethics regarding their use of technology, which most students fail.

motion: Guns should not be purchasable.
text:
For the United States of America especially, guns should not be purchasable. Why? Gun violence would significantly drop. School shootings would stop. Gang violence would slow down.
But what if purchasing a firearm is for self defense? The second amendment is the right to bear arms, everyone knows that, but the robber wouldn't have a gun either. Grab a steak knife and hide. Is it the safest idea? No, I definitely admit that. I'm fairly sure that the second amendment is one of the only reasons, and definitely the predominant one, that guns are purchasable in the United States. 
Now, what about the military? Firearms should be usable in the military only. If someone is caught smuggling one (or attempting to) off military grounds, they'd be punished.
What about hunting, for food or for a sport? In my eyes, hunting is beyond immoral and unjust. If I could have it my way, everyone on the planet would be a vegetarian. Since that's irrational, and this debate isn't about vegetarianism, I'll save that argument. In short, hunting rates would significantly drop in the United States altogether.
Just imagine a utopia where there are next to no school shootings. Significantly less aggravated assaults or murders. Significantly less armed robberies. Less materials wasted on firearms. The list goes on. Keeping guns off the market is the first step to peace throughout the United States.

motion: Should euthanasia or physician-assisted death be legal?
text:
Euthanasia or physician-assisted death should be legal, for a majority of reasons. An example is people with terminal conditions, such as certain types of cancers, heart failure, and advanced Alzheimers's disease. These people should be allowed to decide whether or not they want euthanasia or assisted dying so as to avoid pain and suffering caused by their illness. 

However, while this should be legal, it should also be heavily monitored by professionals and those who do it should have an appropriate amount of time to think it over, and be presented with all possible outcomes.

motion: Can wildlife conservation and human development coexist?
text: With the developments of humanity as a whole, it is often criticized the prioritization of ecology and especially zoological preservation. As humanity continues to expand, more and more of the environment suffers. We loose so much valuable information about not just the animals themselves, but us a species for each individual species that slowly goes extinct. Some argue that for humanity to succeed as a species, the preservation of wildlife can not be a forefront ideology, however this is incorrect. As ideals of expansionism emerged as the United States emerged, so did the ideals of conservation and preservation. As the America expanded and developed new areas were put in place along with laws that specifically protected the animals. Did this hinder or harm the development of that settlement? No. No act of wildlife or ecological conservation as ever severely harmed the development of humanity. It can coexist efficiently and effectively with human development with right implementations.

motion: Should companies implement gender quotas to ensure diversity?
text: I think that forcing an institution, public or private to employ someone simply based off of their gender or any other social classification is pragmatically wrong and ideally wrong. This is because a Business for example should prioritise their productivity levels in the workplace and their employment decisions should be based around the level of productivity and intelligence that a candidate possesses rather than their identity. I understand the consequences of what would likely happen if there were to be no pieces of employment legislation that protected vulnerable social groups such as Women. Employers may target certain groups that are socially advantaged based on their ability to consistently provide a level of productivity for the Business, this is what we see in a lot of employment decisions for a lot of Businesses today. This needs to be fixed pragmatically in a way that doesn't outrightly punish institutions for their employment decisions, but a gender quota to ensure that workplaces are to have equal numbers of Men and Women is practically flawed. While the equality act is a good foundation for further implementations, it can be practically avoided very easily and it is pragmatically ineffective as proven by the levels of productivity in Businesses across Britain not improving after the equality act. Therefore, if this were to be enforced, Institutions would lose.

motion: Is homeschooling better than traditional schooling?
text:
Homeschooling is not better than traditional schooling, because not only are the "teachers" not professional, you dont have any social interaction your whole teenage years. Social interaction is crucial for mental and character development. Furthermore, several studies have reveaeld that children who are homeschooled are more likely to depression than those who are not. 
Not only that, but the teaching is risky. What if the 'teacher' has never taught a day in their life. In traditional schools, we have professional teachers, who knows the exam pattern, questions on the tip of their fingers, because its their daily jobs. But in homeschooling, the schooling is sloppy and unprofessional. Furthermore , several studies have found that homeschooled students are less likely to be successfull than traditionally schooled children.
